title: Where does Malaysia's money go?
subtitle: The federal government's RM407 billion — who gets paid, and what gets built.
question: How does the Malaysian government spend its money?
answer: In 2023 the federal government spent about RM407 billion. RM311bn went to running the country day-to-day — civil servant salaries, subsidies and debt interest — and RM96bn went to building things like roads, schools and hospitals. It collected RM315bn in revenue, so it spent roughly RM91bn more than it earned.

source.notes: Federal government finance for financial year 2023 — the latest full-year actuals published. Figures are split into Operating Expenditure (day-to-day running costs) and Development Expenditure (building assets). Amounts shown in RM billion; source values are in RM million.

trend.title: Total federal spending, 2018–2023
trend.note: Operating plus development expenditure each year, in RM billion. Spending dipped in the pandemic year (2020) then climbed to a record RM407bn in 2023.

operating.title: Operating spending — where it goes (2023)
operating.note: The RM311bn it costs to run the country every year. The single biggest line is civil servant salaries, followed by subsidies & social assistance.

development.title: Development spending — what gets built (2023)
development.note: The RM96bn spent on building the country: infrastructure, public services and defence. 'Economy' covers roads, utilities, transport and industry.

takeaways: Federal spending splits in two: **RM311bn operating** (the cost of running the country day-to-day) and **RM96bn development** (building roads, schools and hospitals).
The biggest single cost is **civil servant salaries at ~RM92bn** — nearly a third of all operating spending — followed by **subsidies & social assistance (~RM78bn)**.
**Debt interest alone was ~RM46bn** in 2023 — more than the government spent building all of Malaysia's social infrastructure that year.
Development money is dominated by the **economy function (~RM57bn)**: roads, utilities, transport and industry.
Spending outran revenue by **~RM91bn**, a gap the government covers by **borrowing** — which is why debt interest keeps climbing.

faq.q: How much does the Malaysian government spend?
faq.a: In 2023 the federal government spent about RM407 billion — roughly RM311 billion in operating expenditure (day-to-day running costs) and RM96 billion in development expenditure (building assets), according to the Ministry of Finance.

faq.q: What does the Malaysian government spend the most on?
faq.a: The single largest item is civil servant salaries (emoluments) at about RM92 billion in 2023, followed by subsidies & social assistance at about RM78 billion.

faq.q: How much does Malaysia pay in debt interest?
faq.a: The federal government paid about RM46 billion in debt service (interest) in 2023 — around 15% of its operating spending.

faq.q: Does Malaysia run a budget deficit?
faq.a: Yes. In 2023 the federal government spent about RM91 billion more than it collected in revenue, a gap funded by borrowing.

faq.q: Where does this data come from?
faq.a: From the Ministry of Finance's Annual Federal Government Finance, published as official open data on data.gov.my. Figures are FY2023 actuals, the latest full year available.
